message.content:
I don’t have real‑time data, but you can quickly check the current air quality in Los Angeles by visiting one of the following trusted sources:

| Source | What it offers | How to use |
|--------|----------------|------------|
| **AirNow** (EPA) | Real‑time AQI, pollutant breakdown (PM₂.₅, PM₁₀, O₃, NO₂, CO) | Go to <https://www.airnow.gov/> → “Find Air Quality” → type “Los Angeles, CA”. |
| **AQICN** (World Air Quality Index) | Global map, hourly updates, health recommendations | Visit <https://aqicn.org/city/los-angeles/>. |
| **Los Angeles County Air Pollution Control District** | Local advisories, long‑term trends | <https://www.lacityair.org/>. |
| **Weather apps** (e.g., Weather.com, AccuWeather) | Often include AQI in the forecast | Search “Los Angeles AQI” in the app. |

### Quick Tips

1. **Look for the AQI value** – it’s a single number that summarizes overall air quality.  
2. **Check the pollutant breakdown** – sometimes a single pollutant (e.g., ozone on a hot day) can drive a poor AQI even if other pollutants are fine.  
3. **Health advice** – most sites give a short recommendation (e.g., “Good”, “Moderate”, “Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups”, etc.).  

If you’re planning outdoor activities, it’s a good idea to check the AQI a few hours before you go, as conditions can change rapidly, especially during heat waves or wildfire smoke events.
